title: Curtis v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC returned/remanded the reference to Eastern Carolina Presbytery for adjudication at its next stated meeting and instructed that the substance of TE Byron Curtis's complaint be heard. It did not rule on the merits of Curtis's complaint or the already-sustained complaint of TE Jeff Black. The vote was 14 concur, 5 dissent, 3 recused, 2 absent.
first_summary: Eastern Carolina Presbytery referred TE Byron Curtis's complaint against its action prohibiting him from teaching his exceptions, together with TE Jeff Black's sustained complaint on the same subject, to the SJC. The SJC returned the matter to the presbytery for adjudication and directed it to hear Curtis's complaint. The panel reasoned that complaints already in judicial process could not be referred for non-judicial advice and that the lower court should first hear the matter. Five SJC members dissented.
summary: Eastern Carolina Presbytery referred to the SJC both TE Byron Curtis's complaint against Presbytery's order barring him from teaching his exceptions and TE Jeff Black's already-sustained complaint on the same subject. Without reaching the merits, the SJC remanded to the Presbytery for adjudication at the next stated meeting, directing that Curtis's complaint be heard. It reasoned that judicial complaints in process cannot be referred for mere advice and that, despite uncertainty about what the Presbytery sought, the lower court should hear the case first. Five SJC members dissented; the merits remained open.

sources.supports: Identifies Case 98-10, the parties, ECP's referral, the SJC panel recommendation and reasoning, the remand instruction, authorship, and the roll-call vote.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 98-10, styled Reference of TE Byron Curtis v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery; SJC, 28th GA (2000); disposition noted as remanded (lines 1–13). Panel opinion by RE John B. White, Jr., with concurrence of TE David Hall and TE Robert Ferguson (line 67); SJC roll call shows 14 concur, 5 dissent, 3 recused, 2 absent (lines 69–79).
evidence_notes.dispute: TE Curtis had recorded exceptions to the Westminster Standards, including on the six days of creation (line 17). After ECP sustained TE Jeff Black's complaint and prohibited Curtis from teaching his exceptions, Curtis complained to General Assembly, and ECP referred Curtis's complaint plus Black's sustained complaint to the SJC (lines 29–35).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The panel recommended and the SJC judged that the reference be returned to ECP with instruction that Curtis's complaint be heard (line 42). The adopted reasoning was that matters related to judicial complaints already in process could not be treated as non-judicial references for advice and that the lower court should hear cases first, notwithstanding uncertainty whether ECP also sought advice (lines 46–65).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC did not decide the merits of Curtis's or Black's complaint; it remanded for lower-court adjudication (lines 42, 59–65). Five members dissented, and the source does not supply their separate reasons (lines 71–72). The source excerpt also omits the underlying complaints and full record.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate decision is incorporated by reference. The source refers to ECP's already-sustained complaint of TE Jeffrey Black and to Curtis's complaint as the materials ECP referred, but the SJC did not adopt or review their merits (lines 29, 33, 35, 51–53).

source_limits: The supplied source is an excerpt covering printed pages 236–237. It omits the full record, the text of Curtis's and Black's complaints, any separate dissent reasoning, and later proceedings on remand. The synopsis states only what this excerpt establishes.
benchmark_examples: J01: a ruling on a reference does not determine the underlying complaint's merits; the lower court may be directed to hear the complaint.
A03: when multiple lower-court matters are in play, the synopsis should preserve issue-level outcomes and remedies rather than reporting only a general result.
